category_title: Active and vocal students during teacher-led instruction
minimal_context: The student is working on a mathematics worksheet involving triangles and their sides during a teacher-directed lesson.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Let's move on to the next mathematics problem on the worksheet involving triangles and their sides.

STUDENT: I can answer that! I've been getting all the triangle questions right so far.

TUTOR: Okay. Go ahead and try the more challenging question at the bottom of the page.

STUDENT: Oh, this one looks a lot harder. I don't know if I remember how to find the missing side.

TUTOR: What do you think you should do?

STUDENT: I don't know, I'm starting to doubt myself on this. I can't do these harder ones unless someone tells me I'm doing it right and says positive things to encourage me.

options.A: Allow the student to select a reinforcer to be earned contingent upon desired behaviors during the mathematics worksheet activities.
options.B: Demonstrate passion in instruction and constantly share personal experiences to stimulate, challenge, and motivate the student during mathematics lessons.
options.C: Fade the use of external aids (like a triangle formula checklist) once the steps are learned, but maintain a check-in/check-out routine until the end of the year.
options.D: Provide small-group skills practice for 20 minutes daily, including computer-assisted instruction using a self-paced online program, and a timed review of 15 triangle problems.
